newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end higher, boosted early by cash.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end higher, boosted early by cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended on the high end of Friday's trading range in lighter volume as the cash market defied the normal drop in weekend demand, industry sources said.

October finished 5.4 cents higher at $1.863 per million British thermal units after hitting a high of $1.88 earlier this afternoon. November widened the gap with October to settle up 6.8 cents at $2.057.
"The market's ability to rally in spite of that shows good strength. Yesterday's rise in open interest shows that there was fresh buying behind the rise," said Tim Evans at Pegasus.
Some traders contend that the lighter volume, coupled with cooler weather forecasts may mean that there is not enough support to the upside.
However, others argue that this may mean that the trend has changed.
"It may mean that there's no strong effort to cap the market. One side of the market has indicated that the other side is taking control," Evans added.
Technically, October support was seen at $1.735 and then at $1.68. Resistance was pegged first in the low-$1.90s, then $1.955.

Cash prices on the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes were talked in the low-to-mid $1.70s, while Midcontinent prices hovered in the high-$1.50s to low-$1.60s. Permian basin prices also held steady in the high-$1.40s.
NYMEX said an estimated 22,086 Henry Hub contracts traded, down from Thursday's tally. The 12-month strip rose 3.4 cents to $2.018.
NYMEX's October Permian contract settled five cents higher at $1.55. An estimated 16 lots traded.
Physicals in the west Texas basin were in the high-$1.40s to about $1.50, flat from Thursday's levels.
On the KCBT, October finished 3.8 cents firmer at $1.613 in fairly light volume. The East/West spread widened by 2.5 cents to 25 cents (NYMEX premium).
In contrast to futures, physical prices at Waha were unchanged in the high-$1.50s to about $1.60.
